detail.longDescription: Did dinosaurs eat seaweed? Fossilised teeth from Texas suggest some may have. Researchers led by Clayton Forster analysed 100-million-year-old enamel from coastal duck-billed dinosaurs. Higher carbon-13 levels suggest they may have eaten washed-up seaweed alongside land plants, unlike other nearby herbivores. https://www. movetheneedle.news/brands/what -dinosaur-teeth-reveal-about-life-on-an-ancient-coast/ # Palaeontology # Dinosaurs # Fossils # MTNWeekend # history # science # prehistoric # research # coast
